questions.question_text: What is the exact output of the nested block structure where variables with identical identifiers undergo sequential mutation across inner and outer scopes?
questions.code:
Integer a = 10, b = 25
Begin Block_1
    Integer a = 30
    b = b + a
    Begin Block_2
        Integer b = 5
        a = a * 2 + b
        Print a, b
    End Block_2
    b = b + a
    Print a, b
End Block_1
Print a, b
questions.explanation: In Block_1, a=30 shadows outer a. b is outer b (25+30=55). In Block_2, b=5 shadows outer b. a refers to Block_1's a: a = 30*2 + 5 = 65. Block_2 prints '65 5'. Exiting Block_2, inner b is destroyed. Outer b was 55, now b = 55 + 65 = 120. Block_1 prints '65 120'. Exiting Block_1, local a is destroyed; outer a=10, outer b=120. Final print: '10 120'.
trace: Block_2: local b = 5; Block_1's a = 30 * 2 + 5 = 65; prints '65 5'
Global: outer a = 10, outer b = 120; prints '10 120'

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Forgot that outer b was mutated by Block_1's updated a (65) after Block_2 exited.
why_other_options_are_wrong.C: Assumed a was reset to 30 after Block_2 exited.
why_other_options_are_wrong.D: Assumed global a was mutated by inner block reassignments.

questions.placement_tip: Keep separate rows for each scope level on paper: verify which variable is local vs outer.

questions.question_text: Trace the values of variables p, q, and r as they pass through consecutive interdependent transformations. What is the final value of 'r'?
questions.code:
Integer p = 14, q = 6, r = 0
p = p + q
q = p - q * 2
if (p > 15 AND q < 10)
    r = (p % q) * 4
    p = p / 2
else
    r = (p / q) * 2
End if
r = r + p - q
Print r
questions.explanation:
1. p = 14 + 6 = 20.
2. q = 20 - (6 * 2) = 20 - 12 = 8.
3. Condition check: p > 15 (20 > 15 is TRUE) AND q < 10 (8 < 10 is TRUE). Both TRUE.
4. If-branch: r = (20 % 8) * 4 = 4 * 4 = 16. p = 20 / 2 = 10.
5. Final statement: r = r + p - q = 16 + 10 - 8 = 18.

why_other_options_are_wrong.A: Used the old value of p (20) instead of updated p (10) in the final line.

questions.placement_tip: Check if an if-branch modifies a variable (p became 10) that is reused immediately after the if block.

questions.question_text: In a compiled language supporting constant folding, a programmer attempts to indirectly modify a constant integer via a memory reference pointer. What is the architectural outcome?
questions.code:
Constant Integer MAX_LIMIT = 100
Pointer ptr = AddressOf(MAX_LIMIT)
*ptr = 200
Integer calc = MAX_LIMIT * 2
Print calc

options.A: 200 (The compiler folds MAX_LIMIT directly into literal 100 at compile-time: 100 * 2 = 200)
options.C: Compilation Error: Cannot take address of constant in any language

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Assumes runtime memory lookup instead of compile-time constant propagation.
why_other_options_are_wrong.C: Taking address of a const variable is syntactically allowed with pointers/casts in C/C++.

questions.question_text: A Caesar cipher encryption shifts characters forward by key = 7, wrapping within uppercase letters 'A' (65) through 'Z' (90). What character is output for letter = 'W'?
questions.code:
Character letter = 'W'
Integer key = 7
Integer shifted = (letter - 'A' + key) % 26
Character cipher = 'A' + shifted
Print cipher
questions.explanation: Letter 'W' has ASCII code 87. letter - 'A' = 87 - 65 = 22 (0-indexed position of W in alphabet). 22 + key = 22 + 7 = 29. 29 % 26 = 3. 'A' + 3 = 65 + 3 = 68, which is the ASCII character for 'D'. Output is 'D'.

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Off-by-one error (assumed 29 % 26 = 2).

questions.question_text: Assume a 16-bit signed integer type in two's complement with range -32,768 to 32,767. If x is initialized to 32,760 and updated via 'x = x + 10', what is the exact evaluated result of 'x < 0'?
questions.code:
Signed16BitInteger x = 32760
x = x + 10
Boolean isNegative = (x < 0)
Print isNegative, x
questions.explanation: Maximum 16-bit signed integer is 32767. When adding 10 to 32760: 32760 + 7 = 32767. Next +1 wraps to -32768, +2 wraps to -32767, +3 wraps to -32766. Thus x becomes -32766, which is strictly negative (< 0). Condition evaluates to TRUE.

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: 32770 cannot fit in 16-bit signed range; overflow wraps to negative.

questions.placement_tip: Signed integer overflow wraps around continuously in two's complement circle: MAX + 1 = MIN.

questions.question_text: What are the final values of variables a, b, and c after evaluating the complex relational condition?
questions.code:
Integer a = 3, b = 7, c = 2
if (++a >= 4 AND (b = b + 3) > 12 OR ++c > 2)
    a = a + 5
End if
Print a, b, c
questions.explanation:
1. ++a: a increments to 4; 4 >= 4 is TRUE.
2. Left of OR has AND: since 4 >= 4 is TRUE, the right operand '(b = b + 3) > 12' must evaluate. b becomes 7 + 3 = 10; 10 > 12 is FALSE. So (TRUE AND FALSE) is FALSE.
3. Because the left of OR is FALSE, the right operand of OR '++c > 2' MUST evaluate. ++c increments c to 3; 3 > 2 is TRUE.
4. Overall condition is TRUE (FALSE OR TRUE = TRUE). If-body executes: a = 4 + 5 = 9.
Final values: a = 9, b = 10, c = 3.
trace: b = b + 3 -> b = 10, 10 > 12 is FALSE -> (TRUE and FALSE) = FALSE
OR requires evaluating right side: ++c -> c = 3, 3 > 2 is TRUE

why_other_options_are_wrong.A: Assumed ++c was short-circuited (it was NOT, because the left side of OR was false!).
why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Skipped mutating b.

questions.placement_tip: In 'A OR B', B is evaluated IF AND ONLY IF A evaluates to FALSE. Trace both branches carefully.

questions.code:

Print result;

options.A: 0 (false, because (10 > 5) evaluates to 1, then (1 > 2) evaluates to 0)
options.B: 1 (true, because 10 is greater than 5 and 5 is greater than 2)
options.C: Compilation Error: Chained relational comparison invalid syntax

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Assumed mathematical transitiveness. In programming, 'a > b > c' does NOT mean 'a > b and b > c'.
why_other_options_are_wrong.C: Chaining relational operators is syntactically valid in C/C++.
why_other_options_are_wrong.D: Associativity and evaluation order are strictly specified by standards.

questions.placement_tip: Remember: In programming, '10 > 5 > 2' is '1 > 2', which evaluates to FALSE (0)!

questions.question_text: What subtle bug exists in the financial balance verification code below?
questions.code:
Float debit = 0.7
Float credit = 0.4 + 0.3
if (debit == credit)
    Print "LEDGER_BALANCED"
else
    Print "AUDIT_DISCREPANCY"
End if

options.B: Prints 'AUDIT_DISCREPANCY' due to binary floating-point rounding error where 0.4 + 0.3 does not equal 0.7 exactly in IEEE-754
options.C: Compilation Error: Cannot compare Float with '=='

questions.explanation: In IEEE-754 floating point (used by C/Java/Python), decimal fractions like 0.7 and 0.3 have infinite binary repeating expansions. 0.4 + 0.3 evaluates to approximately 0.7000000000000001, so 'debit == credit' is FALSE, causing an erroneous 'AUDIT_DISCREPANCY'.
trace: Equality check fails; else branch executes

why_other_options_are_wrong.A: Assumes exact decimal arithmetic in binary floating-point registers.
why_other_options_are_wrong.C: Equality comparison between floats is syntactically legal.
why_other_options_are_wrong.D: Does not throw a runtime exception.

questions.placement_tip: Never test floats with '=='; always use an epsilon tolerance: abs(debit - credit) < 0.0001.

questions.question_text: Trace the execution of variables x, y, and z. Which variables undergo modification?
questions.code:
Integer x = 5, y = 8, z = 12
if ((x > 10 AND ++y > 8) OR (++x > 5 AND ++z > 12))
    x = x + 1
End if
Print x, y, z
questions.explanation:
1. Left of OR: (x > 10 AND ++y > 8). Since x > 10 (5 > 10) is FALSE, short-circuit prevents ++y from running! y remains 8. Left of OR is FALSE.
2. Right of OR: (++x > 5 AND ++z > 12). Since left of OR was FALSE, right side must evaluate.
3. ++x pre-increments x from 5 to 6; 6 > 5 is TRUE.
4. Since first part of AND is TRUE, ++z runs, incrementing z from 12 to 13; 13 > 12 is TRUE.
5. Both parts TRUE, so condition is TRUE. If-body runs: x = 6 + 1 = 7.
Final values: x = 7, y = 8, z = 13.
trace: Right of OR evaluates: ++x -> x = 6, 6 > 5 is TRUE

why_other_options_are_wrong.B: Erroneously incremented y (it was short-circuited).
why_other_options_are_wrong.C: Failed to execute if-body addition x = x + 1.

questions.placement_tip: Carefully track which expressions are short-circuited and which are forced to evaluate.
